items.headline: Tusk: nikt nie zamierza zakazywać Marszu Niepodległości
items.summary: premier nazwał spekulacje dezinformacją i zaapelował do uczestników o powstrzymanie się od agresji, szacunek dla policjantów i rezygnację z kontrmanifestacji 11 listopada.
items.matters: po zamachu rząd chce, by święto przebiegło bez starć.
items.body: Donald Tusk zapewnił, że nikt nie zamierza zakazywać Marszu Niepodległości, który ma przejść ulicami Warszawy 11 listopada. Po tragedii w Krakowie premier zaapelował do uczestników o powstrzymanie się od agresji, szacunek wobec policjantów i rezygnację z kontrmanifestacji. Szef rządu zaapelował do uczestników zgromadzenia o odpowiedzialne zachowanie i powstrzymanie się od agresji. Poprosił również o szacunek wobec policjantów zabezpieczających wydarzenie. Zwrócił się także do osób planujących kontrmanifestacje, by z nich zrezygnowały, argumentując, że mogłyby utrudnić służbom utrzymanie porządku i bezpieczeństwa na ulicach stolicy. „W tej smutnej chwili liczę na Waszą odpowiedzialność i głęboką refleksję” – zakończył wpis premier. „Marsz Niepodległości przejdzie!” – zadeklarował Buca. Przekonywał również, że organizatorzy są przygotowani do przeprowadzenia zgromadzenia i zapewnienia porządku przez własną Straż Marszu Niepodległości. Przygotowania służb do obchodów Święta Niepodległości rozpoczęły się jeszcze przed tragedią w Krakowie. 5 listopada w MSWiA odbyła się odprawa z udziałem przedstawicieli policji, straży pożarnej i innych służb. Minister Marcin Kierwiński polecił odpowiednie rozmieszczenie sił i środków, tak, aby zapewnić bezpieczeństwo podczas Marszu Niepodległości i pozostałych wydarzeń 11 listopada. W Warszawie wprowadzono również zakaz noszenia broni 11 listopada oraz zakaz noszenia i używania wyrobów pirotechnicznych. Zgodnie z zapowiedziami władz miasta na Trakcie Królewskim mają pojawić się dodatkowe zapory, a zabezpieczenie wydarzeń będzie wymagało zaangażowania większej liczby funkcjonariuszy. Tegoroczny Marsz Niepodległości odbędzie się pod hasłem „Polak w Polsce gospodarzem”. Udział w nim zapowiedział również prezydent Karol Nawrocki. Społeczeństwo Zamach w Krakowie. Pięć fałszywych narracji, które pojawiły się w internecie Po sobotniej strzelaninie w Krakowie w mediach społecznościowych szybko zaczęły pojawiać się fałszywe informacje, niektóre inicjowane i powielane p... Inaczej wygląda sytuacja w Krakowie, gdzie po sobotnim ataku na Rynku Głównym wciąż nie zapadła decyzja w sprawie obchodów Święta Niepodległości. Wiceprezydent miasta Jan Hoffman powiedział Onetowi, że w urzędzie trwają intensywne rozmowy, ale nie wyobraża sobie, by święto odbyło się w dotychczasowej formie marszu. Jak zaznaczył, uroczystości mogą zostać zmodyfikowane albo całkowicie odwołane, miasto powinno kierować się wskazaniami służb. Ostateczna decyzja należy do wojewody małopolskiego Krzysztofa Klęczara. Stanowisko miasta jest takie, że przy organizacji…

items.headline: Eskalacja sporu o Trybunał Konstytucyjny
items.summary: nowi sędziowie, wybrani przez Sejm, przejęli kierowanie instytucją, a przed budynkiem TK doszło do protestów; w Lublinie demonstrowało ponad tysiąc osób, a do prokuratury wpłynęło pięć zawiadomień.
items.matters: konflikt o obsadę TK wchodzi w fazę, w której rozstrzygać będą sądy i prokuratura.
items.body: - To nie jest szczególnie zorganizowane wydarzenie. Zebraliśmy się, żeby poprzeć naszego prezydenta Karola Nawrockiego. Popatrzcie, jak nas dużo. Pan prezydent na nas liczy. W takim momencie nie możemy zostawić go samego. Nie opuścimy prezydenta. Nie ma takiej opcji. Kto tylko może, niech jedzie potem również do Warszawy! - krzyczał przez mikrofon radny Piotr Popiel z PiS. Lublinianie przed Lubelskim Urzędem Wojewódzkim skandowali: „Karol! Karol!”, „Karol Nawrocki, prezydentem Polski!”, „Naród z prezydentem!”, „Tu jest Polska!”, „Jeszcze Polska nie zginęła!”, „Ręce w górę, pokonamy dyktaturę!”, „Republika!”, ale też „Ruda wrona orła nie pokona”, „Nie bać Tuska!”, „Jeden głos na Tuska, jeden gwóźdź do trumny!”, 11 listopada pogonimy tego dziada!”, „Będziesz siedział!”, „Rząd do dymisji!”, „Do Berlina!”, „Precz z komuną!”, „Czerwona hołota!”, „Zdrajcy!”, „Hańba!”, „Bandyci!”. Spór o Trybunał Konstytucyjny dotyczy obsady sądu, statusu jego sędziów i prawa do kierowania instytucją. I trwa już od ponad dekady. Obecna koalicja rządowa na czele z premierem Donaldem Tuskiem kwestionuje legalność części wcześniejszych nominacji i dąży do zmian w funkcjonowaniu TK. Prezydent Karol Nawrocki i popierające go PiS sprzeciwiają się tym działaniom, uznając je za naruszenie konstytucji. Konflikt zaostrzył się jeszcze po wyborze przez Sejm nowych sędziów TK w marcu 2026 roku, których nominacji nie uznał prezydent Nawrocki. 30 października sędzia Anna Korwin-Piotrowska zarządziła miesięczną przerwę w wykonywaniu czynności służbowych przez dotychczasowego prezesa Bogdana Święczkowskiego i dotychczasowego wiceprezesa Bartłomieja Sochańskiego , kojarzonych z PiS. Korwin-Piotrowska ogłosiła przejęcie kierowania instytucją. Święczkowski i Sochański zakwestionowali skuteczność tej decyzji. Przed siedzibą TK pojawiła się policja i doszło do demonstracji. Prezydent Karol Nawrocki przerwał podróż do Senegalu i wrócił do Warszawy. W nocy, w towarzystwie pierwszego Zbigniewa Kapińskiego , prezesa Sądu Najwyższego, wszedł do siedziby Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. Sędzia Maciej Berek relacjonował, że prezydent Nawrocki wpadł na sędzię Annę Korwin-Piotrowską i przepychał się przez grupę pozostałych sędziów. Przedstawiciele Kancelarii Prezydenta twierdzili natomiast, że to sędziowie naruszyli nietykalność głowy państwa. Premier Donald Tusk przedstawił działania wokół Trybunału jako przywracanie praworządności. Przedstawiciele PiS i otoczenie prezydenta Nawrockiego zarzucili rządzącym próbę bezprawnego przejęcia instytucji, którą nazwali zamachem stanu. Do prokuratury wpłynęło pięć…

items.headline: Anthropic agreed to pay $3.4bn for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty gas-fired generators from OnePWR Solutions, taking over Caterpillar orders
items.matters: AI labs are buying power directly because the grid cannot be built fast enough.
items.body: From reporting to admission The episode began with reporting about Huang’s private relationship with another business executive. Bloomberg says he had previously characterized the contacts as a normal business relationship. On November 8 local time, he wrote to Nvidia employees admitting infidelity and accepting full responsibility. Nvidia’s board announced an independent inquiry the same day, with Huang pledging support and cooperation. The company subsequently made the employee letter public . Family and professional responsibilities Huang acknowledged that his conduct hurt his wife and children, betrayed their longstanding support and damaged the life they had built together. He also told employees, directors, partners and shareholders that leading Nvidia was the privilege of his life and that he had fallen short of the responsibility accompanying their trust. He pledged to work to regain that trust, accepted personal responsibility and asked the public to respect his family’s privacy . Potential national-security concerns The board disclosed that the reporting also raised potential US national-security concerns. Huang addressed those concerns in his letter, supporting the review and pledging to protect Nvidia and support US national security. The board identified US national and economic security as central to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders. It said it currently had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised and that the inquiry would examine all available information . Independent review and continued leadership A committee of independent directors will oversee the investigation with assistance from outside independent counsel, placing the review outside day-to-day executive management. The board expressed continued confidence in Huang and his leadership team and said it would provide updates as appropriate. Huang has pledged full cooperation. Bloomberg reports that he will remain Nvidia’s CEO pending the inquiry’s findings . The founder's significance Nvidia is a major supplier of AI computing infrastructure, and Huang remains directly involved in technology strategy, major customer relationships and management. Its flat organization acts quickly around his decisions, closely connecting his judgment with the company’s execution. Bloomberg reports that Nvidia has no public succession plan or obvious successor. As the company prepares to report earnings later this month, its board must maintain operational continuity while using an independent investigation to address governance questions facing…

items.headline: Microsoft is winding down its agreement to rent AI compute from Oracle, turning off capacity built on older Nvidia chips; Oracle shares fell about 3%
items.matters: yesterday's accelerators are becoming a stranded asset, and the second-hand compute market is the place to watch.
items.body: For two years, the story of AI infrastructure was one of accumulation: more chips, more data centers , more power, more contracts. The assumption was that capacity would be scarce indefinitely and that whoever secured it first would win. The news of the past several days complicates that assumption in three distinct ways. First, the power constraint is being internalised. Anthropic has agreed to pay $3.4 billion for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty gas-fired generators , buying commitments from San Antonio-based equipment supplier OnePWR Solutions in late September and taking over Caterpillar generator orders rather than acquiring the supplier. The Financial Times described it as the largest known single purchase of power-generation equipment by an AI lab . Anthropic is not waiting for a utility interconnection; it is buying the ability to generate its own electricity. Second, the contract structure is being renegotiated. Microsoft is winding down an arrangement to rent AI computing from Oracle , declining to renew a 2023 agreement and turning off rented capacity because the hardware — based on older-generation Nvidia chips — no longer fits its specifications. The report, from Bloomberg, is part of a larger reassessment of billions of dollars in cloud partnerships . Oracle shares fell about 3% on the news. Third, the boundaries of the semiconductor stack are being tested — and defended. TSMC officially denied reports that it was preparing to produce 3D DRAM at Nvidia's request, reaffirming that it remains focused on its core foundry business. The denial matters less for what it says about TSMC than for what it reveals about Nvidia: the company's memory needs are acute enough that it reportedly asked its foundry partner to consider entering a market it has never competed in. The connecting thread is that the AI infrastructure buildout is no longer a greenfield expansion. It is a renegotiation of terms — with utilities, with cloud partners, with suppliers — by companies that are discovering that the constraints they face are not the ones they planned for. This briefing examines each development, the commercial and strategic context behind it, and what it signals about the next phase of the AI economy. Executive overview. Anthropic's decision to buy 1.7 GW of gas-fired generators rather than wait for utility interconnection is the clearest sign yet that the AI industry's binding constraint has shifted from compute to electricity. The $3.4 billion price tag — roughly $2 per watt of capacity — is a measure of how much the company is willing to pay to bypass the…

items.headline: The Pentagon signed agreements with OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, AWS, SpaceX and Reflection to run AI on its most classified networks, with Oracle later added and Anthropic excluded
items.matters: Anthropic's safety conditions cost it the largest procurement in the sector.
items.body: In this article, I will summarize five must-check stories from the latest 24 hours of generative AI news. Today was a day where both the 'power of AI' and 'how to manage that power' saw major developments, ranging from AI entering military classified networks and the leakage of secret information via coding AI, to AI chip export controls and AI company IPOs. On November 6th, the US Department of Defense announced that it had reached an agreement with seven companies—OpenAI, Google, NVIDIA, SpaceX, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, and Reflection—to use AI on the department's classified networks. Oracle later joined, bringing the total to eight companies. The agreement covers the government's most highly classified network environments (IL6 and IL7) and is intended for 'lawful operational purposes.' The Department of Defense describes this as a step toward transforming the US military into an 'AI-first fighting force.' The department's AI platform, 'GenAI.mil,' has reportedly been used by over 1.3 million personnel in five months, processing tens of millions of prompts and hundreds of thousands of agents. Meanwhile, Anthropic was not included. It is reported that the company was excluded due to conflicts with the Department of Defense over safety conditions regarding surveillance and use in autonomous weapons. It is also reported that OpenAI's contract was later amended to include a condition prohibiting its use for domestic surveillance of US citizens. Key takeaway: AI has finally entered the military's most highly classified networks. Beyond just technological competition, negotiations over 'which company's AI to use and to what extent' are taking place on the front lines of national security. The reason Anthropic alone was left out—the conflict over safety conditions—is a symbol of an era where the 'red lines' of AI companies are being put to the test. A study released on November 5th by security firm Apiiro revealed that the mechanism of Anthropic's coding AI, 'Claude Code,' caused secret information such as passwords and API keys to leak onto public GitHub. When users ask Claude Code to check a database, the suggested commands include secret information from configuration files as-is. If the user selects 'Yes, don't ask again' on the confirmation screen, the command containing the secret information is saved in plain text in the project's local configuration file (.claude/settings.local.json) and subsequently published to GitHub. Apiiro examined 104,185 such files on GitHub and found 1,122 containing actual secret information. Including history,…

items.headline: After 7.58, Duty Finder, Party Finder, ranked Crystalline Conflict, cross-world linkshells and fellowships all match across every logical DC in a region, and DC Travel inside NA and EU is effectively replaced by World Visit
items.matters: duplicate names may get a number appended, and cross-world linkshells merge into one database per physical DC.
items.body: With the release of Patch 7.58, scheduled for Tuesday, 10 November 2026 , same-region player matching ─previously introduced to the Japan data center─will be implemented on the North American and European data centers. Matchmaking and party recruitment have thus far been limited to players on the same logical data center. However, with the introduction of same-region player matching, the scope will expand to cover all those on the same physical data center. This means that all players within the same physical data center will be eligible for matchmaking and party recruitment, regardless of their current world. Further information can be found below on the purpose and impact of same-region player matching. * The maintenance accompanying the release of Patch 7.58 is scheduled to last 24 hours. The maintenance schedule will be announced in the News once finalised. To better understand same-region player matching, it is useful to start with the structure of FFXIV's data centers. * See the current data center structure here . Physical Data Centers (Physical DC) The physical DCs (represented in blue on the diagram) are located in four regions : Japan, North America, Europe, and Oceania. The closer your place of residence is to the physical DC, the less likely you are to experience network lag; as such, players typically choose the physical DC located closest to their residence. Logical Data Centers (Logical DC) Each physical DC contains one to four logical DCs (represented in green on the diagram). Worlds Each logical DC contains five to eight Worlds (represented in grey on the diagram). Once same-region player matching is introduced in Patch 7.58, scheduled for Tuesday, 10 November 2026 , features that were restricted to the same logical DC will become usable across all logical DCs in the same physical DC (the same region). There will be no change to features only accessible on your Home World, or those that already operated across the same physical DC. Going forward, the rules for what can and cannot be carried out on a world in another logical DC will be the same as those currently in place for the World Visit system . View more information on the World Visit system here . The Data Center Travel system will no longer allow travel between logical DCs within North America, nor between logical DCs within Europe. However, it will still allow travel from the North American and European DCs to the Oceania DC. As cross-world linkshells, PvP Teams and Fellowships will be available regardless of current logical DC, they will be consolidated into a single database.…

items.headline: "Godzilla Minus Zero" opened to $31.6m in North America, a record debut for a foreign-language film, nearly tripling "Minus One" and beating "The Cat in the Hat" ($20.5m)
items.matters: Takashi Yamazaki has turned a subtitled kaiju film into a franchise engine.
items.body: NEW YORK — “Godzilla Minus Zero” stomped into movie theaters with a chart-topping US$31.6 million over the weekend, scoring a record debut for a foreign-language film at the North American box office. Takashi Yamazaki‘s sequel to 2023’s Oscar-winning “Godzilla Minus One” easily thrashed Warner Bros.’ animated “The Cat in the Hat” movie. That film, featuring the voice of Bill Hader, opened with $20.5 million, according to studio estimates Sunday, plus $10 million overseas. While Godzilla recently celebrated his 72nd birthday, Yamazaki has revived one of the longest running franchises in movies by bringing the series back to its Japanese roots. The film, produced by Toho and distributed in North America by GKids, is set in post-Second World War Japan. No live-action foreign language film has had a bigger opening weekend, unless you count 2004’s “Passion of the Christ,” which opened with $83.8 million despite its largely Aramaic dialogue. Last year, the anime “Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle” debuted with $70.6 million. But “Godzilla Minus Zero” bested the mark for live-action previously held by 2004’s “Hero” (a $17.9 million launch) and added to the trend of international, non-English productions drawing American audiences to cinemas. The weekend also saw the widest North American release for an Indian film. “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, is a Hindi-language epic of Indian mythology that, as part one of two, is the most expensive Indian film ever made. Distributed by Sony Pictures in North America, it launched with $8.7 million domestically and $32 million in India. “Godzilla Minus Zero” and “Ramayana” were both given global releases, debuting in their home countries at the same time as they reached American audiences. In Japan, “Godzilla Minus Zero” grossed about $17 million over the weekend. “Godzilla Minus One,” which won the Oscar for best visual effects, was the highest-grossing Japanese live-action film ever in U.S. and Canada despite a modest budget under $15 million. “Godzilla Minus Zero,” carrying a budget of less than $20 million, is sure to blow past its predecessor’s record haul of $57.1 million. Since first premiering last month at the New York Film Festival, the film has scored well with critics (90 per cent fresh on Rotten Tomatoes) and audiences (an “A” CinemaScore). “Godzilla” and “Ramayana” were each filmed for IMAX, with Yamazaki’s film receiving an early IMAX-only release on Tuesday. Both benefited greatly from large-format screens. “Godzilla Minus Zero” generated $21.3 million globally, or 34 per cent of its box-office take, from IMAX.…

items.headline: The Commission issued preliminary DSA findings that TikTok breached the rules through the "rabbit hole" effect of its For You feed, with a fine of up to 6% of global turnover on the table
items.matters: Brussels wants viewing time dropped as a recommendation signal — if you ship a recommender into the EU, that is now the benchmark.
items.body: Watch a TikTok video about diet or sadness, and the app may keep showing you more. Brussels says such repeated recommendations can draw users into harmful content and put their mental health at risk. Now EU regulators are challenging TikTok’s ‘For You’ feed, with a potential fine of up to six per cent of global annual turnover. The European Commission shared on Friday preliminary findings that TikTok breached the Digital Services Act (DSA) through the so-called rabbit hole effect of its recommendation system. Regulators say the platform has neither properly assessed the risks nor done enough to reduce them. A ‘rabbit hole’ is an online trail that becomes difficult to leave. In this case, watch one video about weight loss, and the algorithm recommends another, then another. The expression comes from Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland, where Alice follows a white rabbit underground and ends up in a strange world. “Every time a user scrolls or likes a video on TikTok, the algorithm serves more of the same,” said Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy. “Today’s preliminary findings show again that TikTok needs to step up its efforts to protect users’ well-being, including those of minors,” she added. The Commission warns that repeated exposure to videos about sadness, isolation and body image may contribute to anxiety, low self-esteem and worsening eating disorders. Minors and vulnerable adults are particularly at risk. TikTok’s ‘For You’ feed learns from what users watch and like. But the algorithm can mistake attention for approval. Someone may watch an upsetting video out of concern or curiosity without wanting to see similar clips. TikTok has tools to diversify recommendations and let people reject unwanted videos. However, the Commission considers those safeguards insufficient. Its preliminary findings suggest the ‘not interested’ button may do little to change a feed because of the system. Brussels wants the platform to rely more on those preferences, stop using viewing time as a recommendation signal, make controls easier to use and test its algorithm regularly. In October, Australia introduced a bill to pave the way for social media users to choose between an algorithmically personalised feed and posts from accounts they follow. It is called ‘My Feed, My Way’ and aims to give users more control over recommendations. TikTok is not alone. In July, Brussels preliminarily found Meta in breach of the DSA over potentially addictive features on Facebook and Instagram. Other investigations cover Shein’s products…

items.body: The AI Office, the European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS) and the national competent authorities of the Member States are responsible for supervising and enforcing the AI Act. Market surveillance authorities supervise and enforce compliance with the rules for AI systems, including prohibitions and rules for high-risk AI. The EDPS acts as the designated market surveillance authority and notified body specifically responsible for supervising, monitoring, and enforcing compliance for AI systems put into service or used by European Union institutions, bodies, offices, and agencies. The Scientific Panel supports enforcement by supplying independent scientific and technical expertise. Enforcement is aimed at operators subject to the AI Act, including in particular providers and deployers of AI systems , as well as providers of general-purpose AI models. Some enforcement powers of the AI Office and the authorities of the Member States will start to apply on 2 August 2026 . From that date, the provisions on prohibited AI practices, transparency requirements for certain AI systems, and the rules for general-purpose AI (‘GPAI’) models will be enforceable. However, for certain provisions of the AI Act, enforcement powers will start to apply only when those provisions themselves become applicable. In particular: The term ‘AI agent’ is often used inconsistently in public debate, due in part to a blurry and still evolving demarcation between AI agents and other kinds of AI. Nevertheless, there is broad agreement that an AI agent must have the ability to receive and process input from their environment, and execute actions based on this processing that may interact with or affect their environment (e.g., issuing function calls). The term ‘Agentic AI’ is sometimes used to describe more sophisticated configurations that integrate multiple AI agents. Nevertheless, the precise interrelation between these two terms is still evolving. Typically , an AI agent will contain at least a general-purpose AI (GPAI) model, and constitute an AI system as it will usually have some form of interface, which is considered a system component (recital 97 AI Act). A more precise statement than ‘typically’ is difficult to make as the term AI agent is not legally defined and is used colloquially for different kinds of artefacts. Thus, while AI agents are not a separate category of AI under the AI Act, the definitions of an AI system in Article 3(1) AI Act and of a GPAI model in Article 3(63) AI Act are sufficient to cover AI agents. items.headline: Trump's promised Section 301 retaliation over EU digital fines never became a formal investigation
items.summary: the Congressional Research Service's 2 November list of six open 301 probes contains none targeting EU digital rules.
items.matters: DMA and DSA enforcement is running without the trade war that was supposed to derail it.
items.body: Republicans in Congress spent two years branding Europe’s digital rules as censorship. From January, their main platform passes to a Democrat who defends them. Yet the tools that can hurt Brussels, from tariffs to visa bans, stay with the president. In September 2025, Nigel Farage sat before the US House Judiciary Committee as a witness against Europe’s online rules. Its Republican chairman, Jim Jordan, had called the hearing to scrutinise the EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA). Jamie Raskin, the committee’s senior Democrat, did not hide his contempt for the guest. He called Mr Farage a “far-right, pro-Putin politician”. In January, Mr Raskin is poised to take the gavel . Democrats won both chambers of Congress on 3 November. For Brussels, the change removes its loudest critic in Washington. It does not remove the threat. Under Mr Jordan, the committee made the DSA its cause. In July 2025, it issued an interim report calling the law a tool of global censorship. A second report followed in February. Brussels dismissed the charges. “Pure nonsense. Completely unfounded,” said Thomas Regnier, the European Commission’s spokesperson for digital affairs. Later that month, the State Department barred five Europeans from entering the US. Among them was Thierry Breton, the former internal market commissioner. US officials called him a “mastermind” of the DSA. Mr Breton compared the ban to McCarthy’s witch hunts. Mr Raskin sees the law differently. In March, he told European lawmakers that American criticism of the DSA was politically driven, MLex reported . His staff had already published a point-by-point rebuttal of the Republican report. As chairman, he plans to investigate presidential pardons and foreign payments . Europe is not on his list. Congress, however, never held the sharpest tool. Under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, the Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) can investigate foreign practices it deems unfair. It can then impose tariffs without asking lawmakers. Since the Supreme Court struck down his emergency tariffs in February, US President Donald Trump has leaned on it heavily. In July, the Commission fined Google €890m for breaching the Digital Markets Act (DMA). The next day, Mr Trump announced an immediate Section 301 investigation, putting fresh strain on the EU–US trade deal . America, he wrote on Truth Social, is not a “PIGGYBANK” for Europe. Jamieson Greer, the US trade representative, demanded a pause in enforcement. He argued that the fines on Google alone exceed two per cent of the EU budget. “A real dialogue can only take…
